description: This file contains the implementation of the EncounterService interface in the OpenMRS framework. It manages creation, retrieval, updating, voiding, unvoiding, and purging of Encounter objects, along with related entities such as EncounterType, EncounterRole, and handling permissions and visits. The class interacts with Data Access Object (DAO) for database operations and coordinates various OpenMRS services to handle clinical encounter data.

classes.name: EncounterServiceImpl
classes.description: Implementation of the EncounterService interface, providing core logic for managing Encounter entities within the OpenMRS framework.

methods.name: setEncounterDAO
methods.description: Sets the Data Access Object (DAO) used for database interactions related to Encounters.

methods.name: getEncountersByPatient
methods.description: Retrieves encounters for a patient based on a search query string, with an option to include voided encounters.

methods.name: saveEncounter
methods.description: Saves or updates an Encounter, handles permissions, visit creation, and updates related observations, orders, and diagnoses.

methods.name: failIfDeniedToEdit
methods.description: Checks if the current user has permission to edit the given encounter, throws exception if not.

methods.name: createVisitForNewEncounter
methods.description: Assigns a visit to a new encounter using the registered EncounterVisitHandler.

methods.name: requirePrivilege
methods.description: Determines if privileges are required to create or edit an encounter and enforces them.

methods.name: removeGivenObsAndTheirGroupMembersFromEncounter
methods.description: Recursively removes specified observations and their group members from an encounter.

methods.name: addGivenObsAndTheirGroupMembersToEncounter
methods.description: Recursively adds specified observations and their group members to an encounter.

methods.name: getEncounter

methods.name: getEncountersByPatientId

methods.name: purgeEncounter
methods.description: Deletes an encounter with optional cascading delete of observations and orders.
